heroHeadline: Mogadishu Eviction Clashes Injure Ten as UN Begins Sweeping Drawdown of Somalia Support Mission
heroSubtitle: Federal security forces demolishing homes in Mogadishu's Tookiyo neighbourhood clashed with residents overnight into August 23, 2026, injuring nearly ten people and prompting former presidents Farmaajo and Sheikh Sharif to publicly condemn the operation as forced displacement. The day before, South West State's Security Minister publicly called on Kenya to arrest and extradite former Southwest State president Laftagareen, blaming him for the deadliest Baidoa fighting since the SNA's March 2026 takeover — the pre-dawn VBIED assault of August 17. Separately, the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) moved from planning to visible execution of its drawdown the week of August 25: at least 10 civilian AU-UN Information Support Team staff received termination notices effective September 10, and UNSOS began auctioning vehicles, generators and other equipment, as the mission's UNTMIS successor stays on track to complete transition to a standard UN country team by October 31, 2026 amid the looming US funding cutoff after AUSSOM's December 31, 2026 mandate expiry. The drawdown lands atop an already-strained security picture: piracy hit a sixth hijacked vessel since April (the tanker Sibu 1/Seamull, seized in the Gulf of Aden on August 20 with 20 crew aboard), and Somalia's food-insecurity and displacement crises remain acute even as the acute phase of the Baidoa fighting has passed.
